subject.title: [Feature]: Feature Request: Batch Tool Calls + Context Block Management + Plan Enforcement

question: Should OpenClaw pursue any of these requested native core surfaces now: file/search batching, AI-callable context blocks, or runner-enforced submitted plans?
rationale: The request changes core tool schemas, context/session semantics, persisted state, and config/enforcement policy, while repository vision only partially aligns and warns against heavy orchestration or optional capability that can live through plugin/API seams.

options.title: Split For Design Review
options.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and ask maintainers to sponsor narrower design tracks for any surface they want to pursue.

options.title: Route Pieces To Existing Extension Paths
options.body: Defer core changes unless a plugin/API gap is proven, using existing Parallel Search, context-engine, pruning, and plugin seams where adequate.

options.title: Decline Core Direction
options.body: Close the direction if maintainers decide native batching, context-block, and submitted-plan enforcement are not planned for OpenClaw core.

recommendation.title: Split For Design Review
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the umbrella and ask maintainers to sponsor narrower design tracks for any surface they want to pursue.

likelyOwner.reason: This handle has the strongest adjacent history across update_plan, strict-agentic behavior, web-search schema, and current tool registration surfaces.
